On MIUI/HyperOS, installing APKs inside a work profile often hangs on the system installer screen (a known firmware issue). Recommended: clone an app store (e.g. Play Store, RuStore or GetApps) into the work profile and install apps from there. Continue anyway?

Install a root CA (for example, the Russian Ministry of Digital Development root) into the work profile only: government sites will then open in browsers inside the profile. Most apps do not trust user-installed CAs since Android 7, and the personal profile is never touched. Android will show a persistent \"network may be monitored\" notice; that is expected.

Check this fingerprint against the value published by the certificate issuer before installing. The certificate will be trusted only inside the work profile: browsers will open government sites, but most apps ignore user-installed CAs (Android 7+).

Android will set up a second user on the phone, with its own storage and its own accounts. Apps you put there run as usual but cannot see what is installed on the rest of the phone. Any of them can be frozen in one tap: the icon goes, and its notifications and background work stop.\n\nYou will choose the profile\'s isolation level right after it is created.
The profile slot is free: no other profile manager

What apps in the profile can still see

The phone model, the Android version and other device properties. That a VPN is up, even when it runs only in the personal part of the phone: the tunnel itself is visible. Where that tunnel leads stays hidden, because the routing table and the connection list are closed to apps.\n\nA screenshot taken inside the profile stays in the profile storage. NFC payment from an app installed only in the profile does not work on most firmwares.
%1$s: installing APKs inside the profile often hangs. Install apps from a store inside the profile instead.

One system step is left: tap the Gatekeeper notification in the shade. If it is not there, turn off Do Not Disturb and pull the shade down.\n\nThis screen closes itself as soon as the profile starts answering.
%1$s: the system finishing button sometimes flashes for a fraction of a second. Open Settings, Accounts, and check whether the work profile was created.
The profile could not be created

Common causes: the device already has a work profile from another app or an earlier install - Android allows only one; the firmware blocks profile creation; the setup was cancelled on the system screen.\n\nWhat to do: open Settings, Accounts, remove the existing work profile and tap Retry. Removing the profile erases its apps and their data; the personal side is untouched.

No app data, no APKs, no accounts, no certificates. Restoring reinstalls the work apps from the personal profile as fresh copies: their logins and chats do not come back. The work profile itself is not restored either, and neither is the profile key.
Why the system Share does not help

A work profile is a separate Android user. Apps on one side cannot see the other side\'s storage at all, so the system share sheet has nothing to offer: the profiles are not neighbouring folders, they are different users of the same phone.

Open the file picker from the app that needs the file and choose Gatekeeper as the source: the other profile shows up there. Or use the transfer button on the top bar of the app list. The receiving app gets access to that one file and nothing else.

A root CA installed here is trusted by browsers inside the profile. Most apps ignore user-installed CAs since Android 7, and the personal profile is never touched. Android will show a permanent \"network may be monitored\" notice in the profile.
Pick a .crt or .pem file; the fingerprint is shown before anything is installed
Freeze when a VPN comes up
Not pinned: profile traffic goes wherever the system sends it
While the tunnel is down, work apps get no network at all. That is the point: no leak into the open internet, but also no connection until the VPN comes back.
No app inside the profile can act as a VPN

The work copy cannot be uninstalled

While Gatekeeper owns the work profile, Android refuses to remove its copy inside the profile: the button in system settings is greyed out and the request is rejected. A stray tap cannot take the profile with it.
Removing the personal copy is safe
The profile, the cloned apps and their data stay where they are. Install Gatekeeper again and it returns to the same profile: it will ask you to confirm the re-pairing with a code.

A system entry, in settings under accounts, on the Work tab. It deletes the profile with every cloned app, its accounts, its chats and its files. No app can hide or block it, Gatekeeper included: that is reserved for a device owner. There is no undo and no recycle bin.
Settings, the app lists and the auto-freeze list into a file you keep
No app data, no accounts, no files: only settings and package names. Copy anything you want to keep out of the profile first, with File Shuttle or the system file picker.
Keeping the profile across a reinstall

The profile can outlive the app: its ownership may be handed to another app for the duration of the reinstall and handed back afterwards. Verified on a test bench, including a change of signing key. It needs a second, companion app, which this build does not ship yet.

The profile is alive but no longer recognises this copy. That happens when Gatekeeper is reinstalled here or its storage is cleared.

Offers to connect to the other profile when a file manager asks for its files and the link is down
A file manager asked for files from the other profile. Tap to open the link, then repeat the action there.

A file manager that can add a storage location through the system picker (MiXplorer, Total Commander) keeps access to the other profile permanently: add the location, pick Gatekeeper, and it stays in its list. The first time it opens the folder after an idle spell, the link is down and it reports no access - a notification then offers to raise the link, and repeating the action inside the file manager works.

An app inside the profile can see that a VPN is up on the phone, even when the tunnel runs only in the personal part. Where the tunnel leads stays hidden: the routing table and connection list are closed to it. The VPN being up on an Android device cannot be hidden.\n\nThe watch follows the VPN state and freezes the chosen profile apps when it goes up or down: an app that must not observe a network change is kept from running at that moment.
